sn22.84:1.2: Now on that occasion the Venerable Tissa, the Blessed One’s paternal cousin, informed a number of bhikkhus:
sn22.84:1.3: “Friends, my body seems as if it has been drugged, I have become disoriented, the teachings are no longer clear to me. Sloth and torpor persist obsessing my mind. I am leading the holy life dissatisfied, and I have doubt about the teachings.”
sn22.84:2.1: Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported this matter to him.
sn22.84:3.1: The Blessed One then addressed a certain bhikkhu thus:
sn22.84:3.2: “Come, bhikkhu, tell the bhikkhu Tissa in my name that the Teacher calls him.”
sn22.84:3.3: “Yes, venerable sir,” that bhikkhu replied, and he went to the Venerable Tissa and told him:
sn22.84:3.5: “Yes, friend,” the Venerable Tissa replied, and he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to him:
sn22.84:3.6: “Is it true, Tissa, that you informed a number of bhikkhus thus:
sn22.84:3.7: ‘Friends, my body seems as if it were drugged … and I have doubt about the teachings’?”
sn22.84:3.10: if one is not devoid of lust for form, not devoid of desire, affection, thirst, passion, and craving for it, then with the change and alteration of that form, do sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise within?”
sn22.84:4.3: with one who is not devoid of lust for form.
sn22.84:4.4: If one is not devoid of lust for feeling …
sn22.84:5.3: for consciousness, not devoid of desire, affection, thirst, passion, and craving for it, then with the change and alteration of that consciousness, do sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise within?”
sn22.84:6.3: with one who is not devoid of lust for consciousness.
sn22.84:6.5: If one is devoid of lust for form, devoid of desire, affection, thirst, passion, and craving for it, then with the change and alteration of that form, do sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise within?”
sn22.84:7.3: with one who is devoid of lust for form.
sn22.84:7.4: If one is devoid of lust for feeling …
sn22.84:7.7: for consciousness, devoid of desire, affection, thirst, passion, and craving for it, then with the change and alteration of that consciousness, do sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise within?”
sn22.84:8.3: with one who is devoid of lust for consciousness.
sn22.84:8.14: He understands: ‘… there is no more for this state of being.’
sn22.84:9.2: one unskilled in the path, the other skilled in the path.
sn22.84:9.3: The man unskilled in the path would ask the skilled man a question about the path,
sn22.84:9.5: ‘Come, good man, this is the path.
sn22.84:9.7: Go along it a little way and you will see a fork in the road. Avoid the left-hand branch and take the right-hand branch.
sn22.84:9.8: Go a little further and you will see a dense thicket.
sn22.84:9.10: Go a little further and you will see a vast marshy swamp.
sn22.84:9.12: Go a little further and you will see a steep precipice.
sn22.84:9.14: Go a little further and you will see a delightful expanse of level ground.’
sn22.84:10.1: “I have made up this simile, Tissa,
sn22.84:10.2: in order to convey a meaning. This here is the meaning:
sn22.84:10.3: ‘The man unskilled in the path’: this is a designation for the worldling.
sn22.84:10.4: ‘The man skilled in the path’: this is a designation for the Tathagata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
sn22.84:10.5: ‘The forked road’: this is a designation for doubt.
sn22.84:10.6: ‘The left-hand branch’: this is a designation for the wrong eightfold path; that is,
sn22.84:10.8: ‘The right-hand branch’: this is a designation for the Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
sn22.84:10.10: ‘The dense thicket’: this is a designation for ignorance.
sn22.84:10.11: ‘The vast marshy swamp’: this is a designation for sensual pleasures.
sn22.84:10.12: ‘The steep precipice’: this is a designation for despair due to anger.
sn22.84:10.13: ‘The delightful expanse of level ground’: this is a designation for Nibbāna.
sn22.84:10.15: I am here to exhort, I am here to assist, I am here to instruct!”
sn22.84:11.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn22.84:11.2: Elated, the Venerable Tissa delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
